messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: Ozempic Dosing Information:
Ozempic Injection Recommended Dosage:
Start Ozempic with a 0.25 mg subcutaneous injection (injection under the skin) once weekly for 4 weeks.
The 0.25 mg dosage is intended for treatment initiation.
It is not effective for glycemic control.
After 4 weeks on the 0.25 mg dosage, increase the dosage to 0.5 mg once weekly.
If additional glycemic control is needed after at least 4 weeks on the 0.5 mg dosage.
The dosage may be increased to 1 mg once weekly.
If additional glycemic control is needed after at least 4 weeks on the 1 mg dosage, the dosage may be increased.
The dosage may be increased to 2 mg once weekly.
The maximum recommended dosage is 2 mg once weekly.
Administer Ozempic once weekly, on the same day each week, at any time of the day, with or without meals.
The day of weekly administration can be changed if necessary.
The time between two doses must be at least 2 days (>48 hours).
If a dose is missed, administer Ozempic as soon as possible within 5 days after the missed dose.
If more than 5 days have passed, skip the missed dose.
Triplet: ["Ozempic", "has maximum recommended dose", "2 mg once weekly"]

The relation 'has maximum recommended dose' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug should not be used at a dose higher than the one specified by the object entity.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'has maximum dose': The subject drug should not exceed the maximum dose specified by the object entity.
B. 'should be avoided during': The subject drug should not be used during the time period specified by the object entity.
C. 'contraindicated in': The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition or characteristic specified by the object entity.
D. 'not administered via': The subject drug should not be given using the route or method specified by the object entity.
E. 'not substitute for': The subject drug cannot be used as a substitute for the drug specified by the object entity.
F. None of the above.

Answer:
